title: Directus CMS Integration
description:
## Overview

Integrate Directus into the Astro template as an optional build-time CMS path so future sites can start Directus-ready without losing the template's local-first developer experience. The integration should reduce repeated CMS wiring while preserving clean builds when no Directus environment variables are configured.

## Architecture

The integration follows a Content Provider pattern: pages call a unified API such as `getBlogPosts()` and `getLocations()` without knowing whether content came from Directus, cache, or local template content. The provider selects the source per content area using a CMS-preferred fallback chain: Live Directus -> Disk Cache -> Local Content/Fixtures.

Key architectural decisions:

1. Pre-render CMS markdown in provider/normalization code; pages never import raw Directus modules.
2. Use CMS-preferred fallback per content area, independently.
3. Keep Directus optional for local development and template previews; only fail hard when `DIRECTUS_REQUIRED=true`.
4. Use Astro native remote image support instead of custom image download code.
5. Use a custom `rehype-sanitize` schema for CMS markdown security.
6. Validate cache entries against `DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG` to prevent cross-site content contamination.

## Scope

- Directus-backed content in this bead set: `blog_articles`, `blog_categories`, and `cities` mapped to Locations.
- Existing local content remains the offline fallback where available.
- Team and Services stay local-only unless new beads deliberately expand the scope.
- Row-level multi-tenancy uses `site.slug` filtering.
- Public planning text, committed docs, logs, cache metadata, and build artifacts must not expose private Directus hosts, tokens, credentials, or infrastructure hints.

## Authoritative Reference

- Tracked public plan: `docs/directus-integration-plan.md`.
- Local draft/source notes: `prd/PRD.md` is gitignored and is not the source of truth.
- Reference implementation: `arp-astro`, to be inspected for transferable patterns rather than copied blindly.
- Directus connection details: configured only through environment variables and private deployment notes, never committed public text.

## Plan Gate

Phase 1 implementation starts only after Phase 0 closes. Phase 0 verifies this tracked plan and the open Directus beads agree, and that baseline quality gates are known.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Phase 0 is closed before Phase 1 implementation work begins.
- The completed integration preserves no-Directus local builds and previews by default.
- Directus strict mode fails clearly only when `DIRECTUS_REQUIRED=true`.
- No secrets, tokens, concrete Directus instance URLs, or sensitive infrastructure hints are committed, logged, cached in public output, or emitted in build artifacts.
- The final implementation has lint, typecheck, tests, build verification, and token-leak audit coverage appropriate to the touched surface.

title: Phase 1: DX & Config Foundation
description:
## Overview

Foundation phase: developer-facing configuration that every subsequent phase builds on. Sets up environment variable patterns, image handling, diagnostic logging, and gitignore rules. This is intentionally small and self-contained so it can be reviewed and merged independently.

## Why This Phase Exists

Every other phase needs to read DIRECTUS_URL, DIRECTUS_TOKEN, and related values from the environment. Without typed env declarations, TypeScript will flag every import.meta.env access. Without .env.example, developers cloning the template will not know what variables to set. Without remotePatterns in astro.config.mjs, Astro can reject remote CMS images.

The diagnostic logger is here, not in a later phase, because the client, cache, and provider modules all need to log through it from day one. Building it last would mean retrofitting redaction into every console output path.

## Deliverables

1. .env.example - committed, empty placeholders only, with no hosts, tokens, or infrastructure hints.
2. src/env.d.ts - TypeScript declarations for all Directus env vars including DIRECTUS_REQUIRED.
3. .gitignore updates - .cache/ entry for CMS cache payloads.
4. astro.config.mjs - image.remotePatterns using a generic, protocol-only pattern that works with any instance.
5. Diagnostic logger utility - redact() function and structured [directus] prefix logging.

## Security Note

The .env.example file is the most sensitive public artifact in this phase. It must contain only empty values and explanatory comments. Do not include sample hosts, provider domains, token examples, replacement strings, tenant names, or deployment hints. The PR reviewer should verify this character by character.

## PRD Reference

Sections 1.1-1.6 and 2.2

- The requirements in this bead are implemented without expanding scope beyond the named behavior, files, or phase.
- Local template behavior still works when Directus environment variables are unset; strict failures only occur when DIRECTUS_REQUIRED=true or when this bead explicitly scopes strict-mode validation.

title: Add remote image patterns to astro.config.mjs
description:
## Overview

Configure Astro's image optimization to accept remote images from any HTTPS source. This enables Astro's <Image /> component to download, optimize (WebP/AVIF), and include Directus asset images in the static build.

## Requirements

Add to astro.config.mjs:
```javascript
image: {
  remotePatterns: [
    { protocol: 'https' }
  ],
},
```

## Why protocol-only (not domain-specific)

Using just { protocol: 'https' } instead of a hardcoded domain keeps the config generic — it works with ANY Directus instance URL. Hardcoding a concrete private CMS host would:
1. Leak infrastructure info in the public repo
2. Break for anyone using a different Directus instance
3. Require a code change when migrating CMS hosts

## Prerequisite

Directus file permissions must allow public read access to assets used in published content. If assets require auth, Astro's image optimization will fail to download them — this is intentional (fail-safe over fail-open). Documented in PRD Section 9 migration guide.

## Performance Note

First build with remote images will be slower than subsequent builds — Astro caches optimized images in node_modules/.astro/. This is normal and expected.

title: Create diagnostic logger with redact() for all Directus output
description:
## Overview

Build the diagnostic logging utility that all Directus module console output passes through. The core function is redact(); it replaces configured Directus environment values in any string before the string reaches the console.

## Requirements

Create a logging utility, likely src/lib/directus/logger.ts, with:

1. redact(message: string): string
   - Replaces the configured DIRECTUS_URL value with a generic URL mask.
   - Replaces the configured DIRECTUS_TOKEN value with a token mask.
   - Replaces the configured DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG value with a slug mask.
   - Handles empty or undefined env values as a no-op.
   - Handles URL-encoded variants of configured values where practical.

2. logDirectusDiagnostic(stats): void
   - Emits source status: live, cache, local, or not configured.
   - Emits content counts per collection.
   - Emits cache operations: written, read, or rejected.
   - Emits fetch timing.

3. All Directus log functions pass through redact() before console output.

## Why This Is Security-Critical

This is a public repo. Build logs from GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Pages, and Vercel can be visible in PR checks or deployment logs. Error messages from failed API calls can contain the configured CMS host or request details. Without redaction, any build failure could expose infrastructure.

The redact() function is also used by the audit script in Phase 6 and the verify script in Phase 2. Building it early means every module gets redaction from day one.

## Considerations

- redact() should not crash on non-string or empty input.
- The function should be importable from a standalone module with no heavy dependencies.
- Console output format: [directus] prefix for all messages.
- Redacted output must preserve enough context to debug the failure type without printing the original configured value.

  [directus] Site slug: [redacted-site-slug]

title: Phase 2: Core Client & Type Definitions
description:
## Overview

Build the Directus SDK client, all TypeScript type definitions (both raw Directus types and shared view model types), and the test factory infrastructure. This phase produces the type contracts that Phase 3 implements against.

## Why This Phase Exists

The shared view model types (BlogPost, Location, BlogCategory, ImageMeta) are the central contract of the entire integration. Both the local adapter (content/local.ts) and the Directus normalizer (directus/normalize.ts) must produce data conforming to these interfaces. Getting the types right here prevents cascading type errors in every subsequent phase.

The Directus client module encapsulates all SDK interaction — bearer auth, timeout, site-slug filtering, draft mode. No other module should import from @directus/sdk directly.

## Key Design Decisions

- BlogPost has both 'tags: string[]' and 'categories: string[]' (for related posts scoring) AND 'category?: {name, slug}' (for CMS routing). See PRD Section 2.4 for source mapping rationale.
- BlogPost has 'rendered?: {html, headings}' — populated by the provider for CMS posts, undefined for local posts. Pages check this field instead of calling getContentSource(). See Resolved Decision 6.
- BlogPost.content is ALWAYS raw markdown (never HTML). This is a hard constraint because calculateReadingTime() depends on it. See PRD Section 2.4 constraint note.
- ImageMeta type carries width/height from Directus file relations — enables Astro's Image component to skip dimension-detection requests.

description:
## Overview

Build the Directus REST client that encapsulates ALL SDK interaction. No other module should import from @directus/sdk — this is the single point of contact with the CMS.

## Requirements

Create src/lib/directus/client.ts with:

1. isDirectusConfigured(): boolean — checks Boolean(import.meta.env.DIRECTUS_URL)

2. createClient(url, token?) — SDK setup with bearer auth via REST interceptor. Adapted from arp-astro (src/lib/directus.ts lines 67-81).

3. fetchWithTimeout<T>(fn, timeoutMs=15000) — Race-based timeout using AbortController. Adapted from arp-astro lines 83-102.

4. fetchPublishedArticles(timeoutMs?) → DirectusFetchOutcome<DirectusBlogArticle>
   - Filters: status=published, site.slug=DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG
   - Fields: explicit ARTICLE_FIELDS list (pinned, not *)
   - Sort: -date_published
   - Limit: -1 (all)
   - Draft mode: when import.meta.env.DEV, include status='draft' (OR condition)

5. fetchCategories(timeoutMs?) → DirectusFetchOutcome<DirectusBlogCategory>

6. fetchPublishedCities(timeoutMs?) → DirectusFetchOutcome<DirectusCity>

7. isLiveResult<T>() / isError<T>() — Type guards on DirectusFetchOutcome

## Design Decisions

- ARTICLE_FIELDS is an explicit const array listing every field to fetch. This prevents: (a) accidentally fetching sensitive fields, (b) schema changes silently adding unexpected data, (c) over-fetching fields we don't use.
- Bearer auth uses REST interceptor pattern (onRequest callback) rather than the SDK's built-in auth, matching the arp-astro approach.
- Error handling wraps all SDK calls in try/catch and returns DirectusFetchOutcome — never throws. The provider decides what to do with errors.
- Draft mode is client-level, not provider-level, because the filter change happens in the SDK query, not in post-processing.

## Considerations

- The SDK's TypeScript generics are complex. You'll likely need 'as never' casts on readItems calls. This is a known SDK workaround, not a code smell.
- All error messages from this module must pass through redact() (from the diagnostic logger) before reaching the console.
- The site slug is read from import.meta.env.DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG with no default — if empty, queries may return all sites' content (the filter is site.slug._eq='' which matches nothing, so this is safe).

description:
## Overview

Build the asset URL resolution and token safety module. This is a security-critical module — it's the primary defense against Directus tokens appearing in the built HTML output.

## Requirements

Create src/lib/directus/assets.ts with:

1. resolveAssetUrl(file, externalUrl, alt?, options?) → ResolvedAsset | null
   - Dual-source resolution: prefer Directus file relation, fall back to legacy string URL
   - If file (DirectusFile object): resolve to ${DIRECTUS_ASSET_BASE_URL}/assets/${file.id}
   - If externalUrl (string): validate via isSafePublicUrl(), return as-is
   - Extract alt text: explicit alt param > file.description > file.title
   - Extract dimensions: file.width, file.height (from DirectusFile)
   - DIRECTUS_ASSET_BASE_URL falls back to DIRECTUS_URL if not set
   - Returns: { url, alt?, width?, height?, source: 'directus-file' | 'external-url' }

2. isSafePublicUrl(url: string): boolean
   - Reject dangerous protocols: javascript:, data:, vbscript: (case-insensitive)
   - Also check for token leakage (calls isTokenSafe internally)
   - Use regex /^(javascript|data|vbscript):/i for protocol check
   - Handle URL parse failures gracefully (return false)

3. isTokenSafe(url: string): boolean
   - Reject URLs containing access_token or token query parameters
   - Check both parsed URL searchParams and regex fallback for malformed URLs
   - Pattern: /[?&](?:access_token|token)=/i

4. assertNoTokenLeakage(urls: string[]): void
   - Throws if ANY URL in the array fails isTokenSafe()
   - Called during normalization on all resolved asset URLs
   - Error message includes the field name (e.g., 'Token leak detected in og_image URL') but NOT the actual URL value

## Security Design

- assertNoTokenLeakage() is a HARD FAIL — if a token leaks into an asset URL, the build must stop. This is not a warning.
- The error message MUST NOT include the leaked URL (that would log the token). Include only the field name and article slug.
- isSafePublicUrl() is defense-in-depth against CMS content containing dangerous protocol links. The markdown sanitizer (rehype-sanitize) also strips these, but the asset resolver catches them at the data layer.

title: Create markdown renderer with custom sanitization schema
description:
## Overview

Build the unified/remark/rehype markdown rendering pipeline for Directus CMS content. This module is used ONLY for CMS-sourced markdown — local content uses Astro's built-in renderer. The sanitization schema is a security boundary for CMS-authored content.

## Requirements

Create src/lib/directus/markdown.ts with:

1. renderMarkdown(content: string, options?): { html: string, headings: Heading[] }
   - Pipeline: remarkParse → remarkGfm → remarkRehype (allowDangerousHtml: false) → rehypeSanitize (CUSTOM schema) → rehypeSlug → rehypeStringify
   - Heading extraction: collect h2-h4 during processing, return as array for TOC
   - Processor cached at module level (created once per build, reused for all articles)

2. Custom sanitization schema (CRITICAL — do NOT use default):
   The default rehype-sanitize schema strips class attributes, id attributes, and target on links. This breaks syntax highlighting, heading anchors, and external links. Use a custom schema:

   Allowed tags: p, h1-h6, ul, ol, li, strong, em, blockquote, pre, code, hr, br, table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td, img, a, figure, figcaption + GFM: del, ins, details, summary, input

   Allowed attributes:
   - a: href (protocols: http, https, mailto, tel), target, rel
   - img: src (protocols: http, https ONLY — no data: URIs), alt, width, height
   - code: className matching /^language-/ (syntax highlighting)
   - span: className matching /^hljs-/ (Shiki token classes)
   - * (global): id (heading anchors from rehype-slug)

   Stripped: script, style, all on* event handlers, javascript:/data:/vbscript: protocols

## Why allowDangerousHtml: false

The remarkRehype plugin has an allowDangerousHtml option. Setting it to false means raw HTML in markdown source is dropped, not passed through. Since CMS content might contain author-injected HTML, we NEVER pass it through — the sanitizer handles what tags/attributes are allowed. This is defense in depth.

## Why Custom Schema (Not Default)

The default schema from hast-util-sanitize is designed for untrusted user-generated content (like blog comments). It's too restrictive for editorial CMS content:
- Strips className → breaks syntax highlighting classes (language-typescript, hljs-keyword)
- Strips id → breaks rehype-slug heading anchors
- Strips target → breaks external links opening in new tabs
- Strips data: on img src → already handled (good), but also strips some valid patterns

Our custom schema allows these specific patterns while still stripping scripts, styles, and event handlers.

## Considerations

- The processor MUST be cached at module level (not created per article). unified().use().use()... is expensive to set up. Create once, process() many times.
- Called during normalization (normalize.ts), not at page level. The result is stored in BlogPost.rendered.
- Heading extraction should capture depth (2-4), slug (from rehype-slug), and text content.

title: Create disk cache module with slug validation
description:
## Overview

Build the disk cache layer that sits between the Directus client and the content provider. The cache enables offline development, speeds up repeated builds, and serves as the second tier in the CMS-Preferred Fallback Chain (Live → Cache → Local).

## Requirements

Create src/lib/directus/cache.ts with:

1. readCache<T>(collection: string): CachedData<T> | null
   - Reads from CACHE_DIR/directus-{collection}.json
   - Validates the cached site slug matches the current DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG
   - If slugs don't match: log warning, return null (treat as cache miss)
   - If file doesn't exist or is corrupt JSON: return null
   - Returns: { data: T[], cachedAt: string, siteSlug: string }

2. writeCache<T>(collection: string, data: T[], siteSlug: string): void
   - Writes to CACHE_DIR/directus-{collection}.json
   - Creates CACHE_DIR if it doesn't exist (mkdir -p equivalent)
   - Includes siteSlug and cachedAt timestamp in the JSON

3. CachedData<T> interface: { data: T[], cachedAt: string, siteSlug: string }

## Why Slug Validation Is Critical

Without slug validation, this scenario is possible:
1. Developer works on site-A (DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG=site-a), cache populates
2. Developer switches to site-B (DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG=site-b), CMS is down
3. Cache returns site-A content for site-B → content contamination

The slug validation ensures cached data is ONLY used when it matches the current site context. A mismatch is treated as a cache miss and logged.

## Considerations

- CACHE_DIR defaults to .cache if env var not set
- Cache files are JSON — include a _meta field with { version: 1, siteSlug, cachedAt } for future schema evolution
- Cache is ALWAYS cold in Cloudflare Pages production (ephemeral build containers) — this is expected and documented in PRD
- Reading/writing should use fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync (build-time only, sync is fine)
- All log output passes through the diagnostic logger (redact() applied)

title: Rewrite blog detail page [slug].astro for dual rendering
description:
## Overview

This is the most complex single task in the entire integration. The blog detail page must be substantially rewritten to:
1. Get content from the provider (source-agnostic)
2. Handle dual rendering paths (CMS pre-rendered HTML vs Astro native render)
3. Resolve author references to full team data
4. Generate static paths for both local and CMS posts

## Requirements

Rewrite src/pages/blog/[slug].astro:

### getStaticPaths()
- Replace getCollection('blog') with getBlogPosts()
- Map posts to { params: { slug }, props: { post } }
- Each post is a BlogPost object, not CollectionEntry

### Content Rendering (the critical dual path)
```astro
---
// If post has pre-rendered CMS content
if (post.rendered) {
  // Use rendered.html directly — already sanitized by the markdown pipeline
  // Use rendered.headings for TOC
} else {
  // Local content — use Astro's native render()
  // Need to get the entry from the content collection by slug
  const entry = await getEntry('blog', post.slug)
  const { Content, headings } = await entry.render()
}
---
```

### Author Resolution
- post.author is { slug: string } — resolve to full team member data
- Use getEntry('team', post.author.slug) or equivalent
- Handle missing author gracefully (show 'Unknown Author')

### Field Migration Table (from PRD)
- post.data.title → post.title
- post.data.description → post.description
- post.data.pubDate → post.pubDate
- post.data.image → post.image (ImageMeta | string | undefined)
- post.body → post.content (raw markdown, for reading time only)
- render(post) → post.rendered?.html or Astro render()
- getRelatedPosts(post, allPosts) → getRelatedPosts(post) from provider
- post.data.showToc → post.showToc
- post.data.draft → post.isDraft

### Props Passed Down
- PostLayout: title, description, pubDate, image (ImageMeta), isDraft
- SEO: title, description, image, ogImage, twitterImage, seo overrides, canonicalUrl
- BlogPostingLD: title, description, pubDate, image (ImageMeta), author

1. The current page uses CollectionEntry<'blog'> which has a .render() method — BlogPost doesn't

description:
## Overview

Build the normalization module that transforms raw DirectusBlogArticle objects into the shared BlogPost view model. This is the critical bridge between CMS data and page components — it handles date parsing, asset resolution, markdown rendering, SEO computation, and draft detection.

## Requirements

Create src/lib/directus/normalize.ts with:

1. normalizeArticle(raw: DirectusBlogArticle): BlogPost
   Transform each field:
   - slug: raw.slug (passthrough)
   - title: raw.title (passthrough)
   - description: raw.short_description ?? ''
   - pubDate: new Date(raw.date_published ?? raw.date_created)
   - updatedDate: raw.date_updated ? new Date(raw.date_updated) : undefined
   - content: raw.content ?? '' (raw markdown — NOT rendered)
   - rendered: renderMarkdown(raw.content ?? '') → { html, headings }
   - image: resolveAssetUrl(raw.featured_image_file, raw.featured_image, 'Featured image')
   - ogImage: resolveAssetUrl(raw.og_image_file, raw.og_image, 'OG image')
   - twitterImage: resolveAssetUrl(raw.twitter_image_file, raw.twitter_image)
   - author: { slug: raw.author_slug } (deferred resolution — page resolves to full author)
   - tags: [] (deferred — CMS articles don't have tags yet)
   - categories: raw.category ? [raw.category.name] : []
   - category: raw.category ? { name: raw.category.name, slug: raw.category.slug } : undefined
   - isDraft: raw.status === 'draft'
   - seo: { titleTag, metaDescription, canonicalUrl, robots } from raw
   - sitemapEligible: computed from robots + canonicalUrl
   - showToc: true (default for CMS articles)

2. normalizeArticles(raws: DirectusBlogArticle[]): BlogPost[]

  // Use rendered.headings for TOC

title: Create build output audit script for token leakage
description:
## Overview

Create a post-build audit script that scans the entire dist/ output for leaked Directus tokens, URLs, and other sensitive patterns. This is the last line of defense — if token redaction or sanitization failed anywhere, this script catches it.

## Requirements

Create scripts/audit-build.mjs:

1. Scan all files in dist/ recursively (.html, .xml, .json, .js)
2. Search for patterns:
   - DIRECTUS_TOKEN value (from env)
   - DIRECTUS_URL value (from env)
   - DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG value (from env)
   - Generic patterns: access_token=, Bearer , authorization: (case-insensitive)
   - Known Directus URL patterns: /items/, /assets/ with token params

3. Output:
   - If clean: 'Build audit PASSED: no sensitive patterns found in dist/'
   - If found: list each file + line number + pattern type (NOT the actual value)
   - Exit code: 0 if clean, 1 if any findings

4. Integration:
   - Add as postbuild script in package.json: 'postbuild': 'node scripts/audit-build.mjs'
   - Runs automatically after every 'pnpm build'

## Why Post-Build (Not Just Runtime)

Runtime redaction (redact() in logger) protects console output. The build audit protects the DEPLOYED output. Even if redaction works perfectly, a bug in asset resolution or markdown rendering could embed a token in an HTML attribute or JSON-LD block. The audit catches what runtime missed.

## Considerations

- Must handle binary files gracefully (skip images, fonts)
- Scan only text-based files: .html, .xml, .json, .js, .css, .txt
- Performance: dist/ is typically small (<100 files for a static site) — brute force scan is fine
- The script reads env vars to know what patterns to search for — if env vars aren't set, it still searches for generic patterns (access_token=, etc.)
- Exit code 1 blocks deployment in CI pipelines

description:
## Overview

Create a comprehensive E2E test suite that builds the site under multiple environment configurations and validates the output. This is the ultimate integration test: it proves the system works end to end, from env vars through the provider to generated HTML.

The existing tests/build.test.ts verifies a single build succeeds. This suite tests multiple configurations: local-only, CMS-live when CI secrets are available, CMS-unreachable fallback, and strict-mode failure. It also validates output content, not just exit codes.

## Requirements

Create tests/e2e/build-integration.test.ts.

### Scenario 1: Local-Only Mode

Config: DIRECTUS_URL is empty and all other DIRECTUS_* vars are empty.
Expected:
- Build succeeds.
- dist/blog/index.html exists and contains local post titles.
- dist/rss.xml is valid XML with item entries.
- dist/ contains no Directus URLs or tokens.
- [directus] logs show not configured and using local content.

### Scenario 2: CMS-Live Mode

Config: DIRECTUS_URL, DIRECTUS_TOKEN, and DIRECTUS_SITE_SLUG are set from CI secrets or a developer environment.
Expected, when CMS is reachable:
- Build succeeds.
- dist/blog/ contains CMS article pages from Directus slugs.
- CMS post pages contain rendered HTML, not raw markdown.
- dist/ contains no tokens.
- .cache/ is created with directus-blog.json.
- [directus] logs show live connected source.
Skip when Directus env vars are not set in CI.

### Scenario 3: CMS-Unreachable Fallback

Config: DIRECTUS_URL is set to a generated unreachable fixture URL and DIRECTUS_TOKEN is set to a non-sensitive fixture token.
Expected:
- Build succeeds by falling back to local content.
- dist/blog/ contains local post pages, not CMS pages.
- [directus] logs show fetch error and fallback message.
- Build does not hang; timeout is enforced.

### Scenario 4: Strict Mode Failure

Config: DIRECTUS_URL is set to a generated unreachable fixture URL and DIRECTUS_REQUIRED=true.
Expected:
- Build fails with non-zero exit.
- Error message mentions that Directus CMS is required but unreachable.
- Error message does not contain the fixture URL or token.

### Scenario 5: Token Leakage Audit

Config: same as Scenario 2 when CMS env vars are available.
Expected:
- Run scripts/audit-build.mjs against dist/.
- Exit 0 with no findings.
- Scan generated text artifacts for configured token values and generic token-bearing URL patterns.

## Implementation Notes

1. Each scenario runs in a subprocess with modified env vars.
2. Use separate temp dirs for dist/ output between scenarios to prevent cross-contamination.
3. Set generous timeouts, about 120s per build.
4. The existing tests/build.test.ts can remain as a quick smoke test.

## Logging Requirements

- Log each scenario start.
- Log env vars in redacted form.
- Log build command and duration.
- Log each assertion with PASS/FAIL context.
- Log scenario summaries and final suite summary.
